meaning: The comment interprets Fig. 7 of Ursino & Lodi (1997): SAP drops from 100 to 90 mmHg over t=10-20 s and then stays at 90 for the whole run, so the later ICP fall near t=250 s is read as a model-generated plateau wave rather than a change in the input. That reading is what fixes the step input Pa_of(t) at line 311.

could_move.what: Pa_of(t) holds SAP at 90 mmHg for all t>20; if the paper instead restored SAP, this input and every fig7 trace would change
The claim that the t≈250 s ICP fall is an intrinsic plateau wave, not input-driven — this is the qualitative conclusion the figure is used to support
The six kE values swept in fig7 are compared under this single input assumption, so the stability claim across kE rests on it

expectation: Unknown in size. Direction: if SAP were actually restored toward 100 mmHg after the ramp, ICP would be expected to rise again rather than fall, and the t≈250 s feature would no longer be attributable to the model. I cannot tell from the context which reading is correct; the reach trace shows no other references, so the blast radius looks local to fig7, but I cannot confirm that.

check.why: Re-runs only the Fig. 7 case so the ICP trace near t=250 s can be eyeballed against the published figure, without a full re-fit.
